conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Mousetrap Chain
style.description: The classic chain-reaction demonstration on a bright blue sports-hall floor: a neat grid of toy-scale spring traps (pale wooden board, yellow pedal, red paddle hammer), each loaded with two white ping-pong balls. One orange ball is bounced in, trips one trap, which flings two balls, which trip two more — one, two, four, eight — until the whole floor erupts in a storm of flying balls and settles with every trap sprung. A seeded planner precomputes every landing, ballistic arc and snap; the same plan drives the picture, the snaps and ball ticks in the score, and a row of dots that doubles generation by generation.

map.description: faint mottling of a poured blue sports floor

motion: Snap: a trap's red paddle swings 180 degrees from the back half onto the yellow pedal in under 0.1 s with a small rebound; the board hops and stays slightly shoved out of line.
Throw: the two balls on the paddle leave on closed-form ballistic arcs, each aimed at a set trap nobody else is aiming at, so generations double until traps run out.
Bounce: every ball takes up to three damped bounces and a decelerating roll to rest; early generations steer into the aisles, late ones trip traps by accident.
Eruption: with no set traps left to aim at, balls are lobbed high and wide; the camera is locked for the whole storm.
Coda: the last ball to land dribbles on alone, then silence with every trap sprung.
Camera: starts close on one trap, pulls back generation by generation to reveal the whole floor, then holds.

notes.mechanism: cascade.js simulates the chain once (seeded, event-driven): a landing on a set trap snaps it and throws its two balls, each aimed at a set trap nobody else is aiming at; closed-form ballistic legs, damped bounces, a roll to rest.
